title: 📰 AI news · October 16
takeaway: Today’s news shows where project keys live: GitHub projects were scanned for AI service keys, and the agent platform Langflow is attacked through connection settings. Recommendation: check where your project and bot keys are stored and replace the ones you haven’t changed in a long time.
cta: 🔐 Check where my keys are stored

items.title: About 1,900 GitHub accounts were hacked
items.text: Attackers added a file named like “security-audit” to projects; it hunted for passwords, cloud access and AI service keys. If your project lives on GitHub, keys in it are the main target, and old keys stay at risk. Check where your project’s keys are stored: in code, notes or chats.

items.title: The AI-agent platform Langflow is already being attacked
items.text: In Langflow any logged-in user could run commands on the server by adding their own MCP server. Since September 19 there have been 1,423 attack attempts, going after the secret key and admin password in the settings. If you build agents, your keys sit in similar settings. Check your version: the fix is in 1.9.0.

items.title: Spyware was delivered through ordinary ads
items.text: Citizen Lab showed that a script in ads sent a device’s address and ad ID, and the server sent an attack only to chosen targets, with no click needed. At least 45 Al Jazeera devices were infected. If you handle sensitive data, make sure your phone and browser are up to date.

items.title: Android gets AI protection against scams
items.text: Google Messages will analyze suspicious chats with Gemini, Gemini Nano will check links from strangers on the phone, and apps can no longer quietly enable call forwarding. Bank call verification has already stopped over 3 million fraudulent calls. Check Google Messages settings: cloud analysis is switched on manually.

items.title: Meta released the open model Muse Spark Open
items.text: It has 816 billion parameters with 42 billion active at once and a one-million-token context. Built for code and agent tasks, with open weights on Hugging Face. It runs on two Mac Studios with 512 GB of memory each.

items.title: GPT-6-Astra solved 49 of 50 physics problems
items.text: Thirty-five researchers built 50 new problems with verifiable answers. Astra scored 98% and Opus 5.5 in Claude Code scored 92%. A solution cost under three dollars on average.

items.title: FLUX 3 Klein runs on an ordinary graphics card
items.text: The open model creates and edits images in 4K and accepts up to ten references. The compressed version runs on 8 GB of video memory and makes an image in under 9 seconds on an RTX 4070.

items.title: Google launched Universal Cart in the US
items.text: A shared cart for Search and Gemini collects products from different stores, flags price drops and suggests promo codes. Checkout runs on a protocol that helps AI agents and stores work together.

items.title: Amazon released two Bee AI devices
items.text: Bee Frontier ($74.99) is worn on the wrist or clothing; it listens to conversations and produces summaries, to-do lists and calendar invites. Bee Eclipse ($99.99) attaches to a phone and arrives later.
